title: Simulation - Low/High Resolution
content:
Hello everyone,

I am investigating garment pressure values in CLO3D and have noticed a significant effect of mesh resolution on the results.

Using the same garment and avatar, the **High Resolution** simulation produces pressure values that are much higher (sometimes nearly double) than those obtained with **Low Resolution**. This is surprising because I would expect the higher-resolution simulation to provide results closer to our experimental measurements, but the opposite seems to occur.

Does anyone know:

  * How CLO3D calculates garment pressure?

  * Why pressure values can change so significantly with mesh resolution?




Any insights or references would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you!

![1c500cce0252460791802eb217a8c209](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/eb7828705e6f40ac96f266a3c35c3049/images/1c500cce0252460791802eb217a8c209Picture1.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi! Can you specify your settings on Low Resolution? In general, from our side that means PD = 5, Avatar Skin Offset = 0, and Collision Thickness of pattern pieces = 1. The difference arises from closer surface contact through less air buffer and the ability of the pattern pieces to wrap more correctly when the PD is lower. Could you please also confirm whether the fabrics you are using for testing are didigtal/physical twins of each other?
content_description: This page seeks to understand how mesh resolution affects garment pressure calculations in CLO3D and to gather insights on the underlying simulation methods.

title: Puckering visualization
content:
Puckering feature allows to specify among other parameters, Density and Width.   
  
In real world, a Puckering vanishes as it goes away from the seam.  
  
Currently, CLO Puckering effect is fixed, I mean, it has the same 3d deep from seam line to specified width.

It would be nice to have a option to specify a point after which the puchering effect vahishes.

Let's say I specify a puckering width of 1 cm and I want it to start vahishing once it reaches 0.5 cm. So, it would looks like this:  
  
Width(cm): 1.00  
Vanishing point (cm): 0.5![9db5d9094a694c06a9172b4c7d51ca9d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/017f2cb7f7f34e78a5cbeb930e522d03/images/9db5d9094a694c06a9172b4c7d51ca9ddefault_puckering.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi, thank you for taking the time to share your feedback with us. We will submit this to our development teams as a feature request. As a temporary workaround, you can also manually fade the puckering normal map using an external image editing software. You can retrieve the normal map file by clicking on the icon as shown on the screenshot.
content_description: This page explains how to customize the puckering effect in CLO by specifying density, width, and a vanishing point for a more realistic seam appearance.
